rationale: C08 is a direct and material drafting template for the child. Both proclamations concern supplemental imports of long-staple cotton under section 22, modify the same 1939 proclamation after a Tariff Commission supplemental investigation, and follow essentially the same sequence of recitals, findings, and operative language. The child updates the quota year, quantity, and narrower cotton specifications while retaining extensive distinctive language and the same administrative machinery. C05 is also closely related to the same regulatory lineage and supplied some recurring language, but it changes the quota year rather than establishing a supplemental quota. C03 shares quota terminology but concerns different legal machinery and is substantially weaker.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the United States Tariff Commission has made a supplemental investigation to determine whether changed circumstances require the modification of the said proclamation of September 5, 1939
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the United States Tariff Commission has made a supplemental investigation to determine whether the circumstances requiring the import quotas...continue to exist, or whether changed circumstances require the modification of the quotas
shared_material.explanation: Both use a Tariff Commission supplemental investigation and changed-circumstances finding as the predicate for modifying the same cotton quota proclamation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: after due notice, a public hearing was held on July 18, 1950, at which parties interested were given opportunity to be present, to produce evidence, and to be heard, and, in addition to the hearing, the Commission made such investigation as it deemed necessary for a full disclosure and presentation of the facts
shared_material.parent_excerpt: after due notice, a public hearing was held on February 17, 1948, at which parties interested were given opportunity to be present, to produce evidence, and to be heard, and, in addition to the hearing, the Commission made such investigation as it deemed necessary for a full disclosure and presentation of the facts
shared_material.explanation: This is nearly verbatim distinctive procedural language, with only the hearing date changed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby find and declare...that changed circumstances require the modification...so as to permit the entry for consumption, or withdrawal from warehouse for consumption...of 1,500,000 pounds...in addition to the quantity...the entry of which has already been made
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby find and declare...that changed circumstances require the modification...so as to permit the entry for consumption, or withdrawal from warehouse for consumption...up to a total of 18,000,000 pounds, in addition to the quantity...the entry of which has already been made
shared_material.explanation: The central operative finding uses the same structure and much of the same language, adapted to a new quantity, quota year, and cotton specification.

shared_material.child_excerpt: without rendering or tending to render ineffective or materially interfering with the domestic program undertaken with respect to cotton, or reducing substantially the amount of any product processed in the United States from cotton produced in the United States
shared_material.parent_excerpt: without rendering or tending to render ineffective or materially interfering with the domestic program undertaken with respect to cotton, or reducing substantially the amount of any product processed in the United States from cotton produced in the United States
shared_material.explanation: The child reproduces this substantive statutory finding verbatim, reinforcing direct template reuse rather than mere topical similarity.
